      <description><p>After a week of alarming warnings about artificial intelligenceΓÇÖs potential to destroy the world as we know it, our technology reporters are answering your questions on the reality of the AI threat live now</p><p></p><p><strong><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/community/live/2026/sep/18/could-ai-really-end-humanity-technology-qanda#comment-175632805">IcommentthereforeIam</a> asks:</strong> Given our senses, emotions, memory and moods, is it ever going to be accepted that humanly conscious AI is fantasy?</p><p><em><strong>Dan:</strong></em><strong> </strong>This is a serious question that has even rattled Richard Dawkins, the evolutionary biologist. He may not believe that God is real but he does believe that AI is conscious - or at least the chatbot he was using, which he called Claudia. ΓÇ£You may not know you are conscious, but you bloody well are,ΓÇ¥ he wrote.</p><p>And heΓÇÖs not the first. In 2022 Google fired an engineer who went public with his belief that a company-developed AI had feelings. At the more troubling end of this belief, there are countless examples of people becoming overly attached to, and influenced by, AI chatbots ΓÇô including cases of psychosis.</p><p><strong>Aisha: </strong>ThereΓÇÖs certainly a theatrical ΓÇô even <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/sep/10/anthropic-researchers-warn-ai-musk">ΓÇ£psy-opΓÇ¥</a>- quality to the flurry of AI doomsaying over the past weeks. We know that the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/jul/22/openai-says-its-models-went-rogue-and-hacked-startup-in-unprecedented-incident">Hugging Face incident</a>, where a ΓÇ£swarmΓÇ¥ of AI agents hacked another company, has been one trigger of the drama. But any company of their size, and with their potential liabilities, would be angling hard to be regulated as favourably as possible. ThatΓÇÖs what big companies do.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/community/live/2026/sep/18/could-ai-really-end-humanity-technology-qanda">Continue reading...</a></description>
